knowledgeAnswers.rationale: The lesson says to divide the total costs by billable hours, so the costs and income are recovered from work that can be billed. Dividing by all paid hours or copying a competitor's or website's rate does not do this.
The lesson says travel and set-up do not shrink with the size of the task, so a minimum charge covers the time needed to attend the site and start work.

The lesson says to build the base rate from your own costs and billable hours, then compare it with the local evidence you can verify. A national average, a friend's rate or one bidding listing is not a sound source.

practicalCriteria: Learner calculates billable hours from a one-month log, showing each non-billable deduction.
Learner builds a base rate from a worksheet of annual costs and an income target, showing the calculation.
Learner sets a minimum charge for a short job and writes the wording the client will see before the visit.
passRule: 80% on knowledge checks; practical sign-off separate
stopWorkCriteria: Stop work if procedure step 1 is not done: Estimate the paid working hours in a year, then subtract travel, admin, marketing, training and leave to find the billable hours.
